add_characteristics.text: The Love Junkies (McKenna, Lindsey, Rose) on 'Girl Crush': the title came first with no agreed meaning. Lindsey's sung opening, played by ear in 6/8, chose the angle. The writers' only check was whether the jealousy made sense (they never imagined the same-sex reading). The phone memo was kept instead of making a demo, and McKenna praises the band's restraint on the record.
'Girl Crush' states its misleadable title in line one and settles it with a plain reason in the chorus (an explanation payoff). Five-stanza form, no bridge.

add_characteristics.text: Zach Bryan is the sole-writer outlier. 'Something in the Orange' (2022-04-22) is an image title that began, on his first account, from the word 'orange'. The title is a frame whose verdict changes from hope to loss. No pre-chorus or bridge. Vocal and guitar were tracked live with light overdubs, in a day. It reached Hot 100 No. 10 without country radio. His origin stories conflict: a cabin sunset, or being stood up on a date.
add_characteristics.evidence: documented_statement, relayed (SC-S16, SC-S17, CW-S49; producer CW-S48); observable_feature (SC-S14, SC-S15)

coverage: These additions rest on two songs: 'Girl Crush' (2014, a Nashville trio writing for a band) and 'Something in the Orange' (2022, a sole writer outside the radio system). Neither is from the Morgan Wallen catalogue the profile is built on; they widen its comparison group and do not describe Wallen's room. They fill the profile's missing release date for 'Something in the Orange': 2022-04-22 (SC-S16, SC-S19).
